reviews.title: Numbers = 5 stars, Mounting = 1 star
reviews.name: dirk
reviews.review:
The numbers themselves are awesome! I love the font, they are beefy aluminum. The waterjet/laser cuts are clean and the faces had a nice even finish (brushed aluminum) They look really nice against my Cumaru siding.

The downside is the mounting design. This may work for smaller numbers, but not very well for the 8″ (and larger I assume unless you add more mounting points/larger studs).

There is a combination of things to make the mounting better. The studs should either thread into the holes in the back of the numbers OR the hole in the back of the numbers should be a tight press fit to the 3/16″ stud (better yet use a 1/4″ stud for the larger numbers). The way it is now, there is a sloppy hole for the stud on the number and it relies on a thin layer of epoxy to hold the stud to the number. If you put too much epoxy on the hydraulic pressure will push the stud out of the hole. so you can only use the slightest amount. Trying to install (hammer) into the wall holes while the number is trying to eject itself out of the other end of the stud is not a good design. Once on the wall, there is no easy way to clamp the number to the stud until the epoxy sets up. The stud to number connection really needs to be a tight fit (pressed in or threaded) for longevity. Also with only 2 studs for most numbers (2,5,3) centered when you clean them if you press too hard on one side of the number or the other it will pop the epoxy connection and make the number loose or fall off completely. The mounting is not a good long term option and for such a high quality product it is disappointing and frustrating. I hope you take my criticism to heart to make your product that much better.

The mounting studs and spacers appeared to be stainless steel which is a nice touch but that is not noted in their advertising description. The paper pattern for drilling holes is well done but I think if I had to do it again I might glue the pattern to a flat piece of cardboard to make it easier to handle. I glued my studs and spacers onto the numbers, as well as installed the numbers into their stud holes, with Gluemasters Thick “Pro Grade” Cyanoacrylate Super Glue with a tapered flow tip bottle and that worked well for me being was easier than mixing epoxy.

reviews.title: Awesome numbers! Hard installation!
reviews.name: Karina
reviews.review: We live in a new build community where they don’t paint the curb numbers. Some neighbors have some painted. The majority do not. But no one has modern house numbers painted on their curb! I love the way it turned out! Large numbers that pop out with the white background we chose. My only complaint is just how difficult it is to install!! Yeah peeling off the backing is easy. Placing it on the curb is easy. BUT removing the top film while keeping the sticker on the curb? That’s a whole different story. First, the sticker doesn’t still well on the concrete. Feels like something that would be made for sticking to a glass window or something. So I needed my husband to really help me hold it in place while I tried remove that top film. Also, I recommended flattening out the number a week prior to putting it on. Like under a stack of books! Really helped us! So: beautiful numbers! Hard application!

reviews.review: When we purchased our home here in Hawai’i, we knew that we’d have to repaint very soon because the weather at 3k elevation is very wet and windy. We began that job by removing the old rusted numbers that were hammered in to the eave face and I began my search for new ones that matched my personality and taste. I was very excited when I found not only brown powder coated numbers, but also the gorgeous Santa Barbara font, AND my address has a dash in it and I had a heck of a time finding a company that provided that small but important detail. I also purchased vinyl decal numbers that matched for my trash cans, and when they didn’t stick to the marbled surface of the plastic, they offered me another set, but suggested that it might not stick and would I prefer a refund, which I did. I had some issues with the epoxy because I’m clumsy and lumbering when it comes to things like that, but after a little clean up and my wife’s more detailed sense of things, they are perfectly displayed and honestly, every time I pull into my driveway I have a renewed sense of pride looking at them.
